subject: Numeracy
title: Counting to five with real things
subtopics: Touch and count four and five
objectives: Children will count up to five objects with one touch for each.
Children will say how many using the last number word.
content: Counting four and five real objects by touching each one once, answering how many, and counting while moving.
teachingActivities: Count slowly with a clear touch and slide for every object; repeat the last number as the answer; keep groups small and lined up.
learnerActivities: Touch and move objects one at a time, count four and five, say how many, and count while moving.
assessment: Check one-to-one touching, order of number words and whether the child says how many with the last number.
expectedOutcomes: Counts up to three objects reliably and up to five with support.
crossCurricular: Physical Development: moving objects one at a time
Social Habits: taking turns to count

lessons.title: Touch, slide and count four and five
lessons.subject: Numeracy
lessons.subtopic: Touch and count four and five
objectives: Children will touch and slide each of four or five objects while saying the numbers in order.
successCriteria: Says the numbers in order up to four or five
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can say the numbers to five in rhymes and count up to three objects by touching each one.
lessons.starter: Show five blocks in a line. Say "I have blocks. How many? Let us count them one at a time and slide them." Touch the first block.
teacherActivities: Touch and slide each block to the second tray as you say the numbers one to four slowly.
Add a fifth block and count again to five. Say "Five blocks. There are five."
Invite a child to touch and slide while the group counts aloud.
Count again from the other end of the line and ask "Is it still five?"
learnerActivities: Children watch and say the numbers with you.
Children say "five" and show five fingers.
Child touches and slides each block while the others say the numbers.
Children nod or say "five" to show it is the same.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Touch and slide each block to the second tray as you say the numbers one to four slowly. Children: Children watch and say the numbers with you.
Step 2. Teacher: Add a fifth block and count again to five. Say "Five blocks. There are five." Children: Children say "five" and show five fingers.
Step 3. Teacher: Invite a child to touch and slide while the group counts aloud. Children: Child touches and slides each block while the others say the numbers.
Step 4. Teacher: Count again from the other end of the line and ask "Is it still five?" Children: Children nod or say "five" to show it is the same.

practical.title: Block slide count
steps: Give each pair a tray of blocks and an empty tray.
One child slides and says each number; the partner shows the fingers.
Swap roles and try four, then five blocks.
practical.safety: Use blocks larger than a child’s fist. Keep trays on the floor with children seated.

differentiation.support: Count only to three and guide the child’s finger touch by touch.
differentiation.extension: Count to five and then show the number on a numeral card without help.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: How many blocks are on the tray?
Can you touch each block just once?

expectedOutcomes: Counts four and five objects with one touch for each
Says the last number as the answer
lessons.conclusion: Slide all the blocks back saying "five, four, three, two, one, home."
lessons.homeConnection: Count five spoons or five shoes at home by touching and sliding each one.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "touch and slide each of four or five objects while saying the numbers in order" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

learnerFacing.songOrRhyme: Touch one, touch two, touch three, touch four, touch five, blocks and me.

lessons.title: Five fruits in the basket
lessons.subject: Numeracy
lessons.subtopic: Touch and count four and five
objectives: Children will count five toy fruits into a basket and say how many.
successCriteria: Counts fruits one at a time into the basket
Says how many when all are in
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can say the numbers to five in rhymes and count up to three objects by touching each one.
resources: Five toy fruits (orange, mango, banana, pawpaw, lemon)
lessons.starter: Spread a market cloth and place five fruits in a row. Say "A market stall! Let us put the fruits into the basket and count."
teacherActivities: Pick up one fruit, name it, and put it in the basket saying "one". Continue to five.
Ask "How many fruits are in the basket?" Wait.
Take the fruits out one by one and count them again.
Ask each child to put in three fruits and say how many, then five.
learnerActivities: Children watch and say the numbers.
Children say or show five.
Children count the fruits as they come out.
Child places the fruits and counts them.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Pick up one fruit, name it, and put it in the basket saying "one". Continue to five. Children: Children watch and say the numbers.
Step 2. Teacher: Ask "How many fruits are in the basket?" Wait. Children: Children say or show five.
Step 3. Teacher: Take the fruits out one by one and count them again. Children: Children count the fruits as they come out.
Step 4. Teacher: Ask each child to put in three fruits and say how many, then five. Children: Child places the fruits and counts them.

practical.title: Fruit basket count
steps: Give each pair a basket and five toy fruits.
One child counts fruits into the basket; the other checks by counting again.
practical.safety: Toy fruits must be bigger than a child’s fist. Do not use real small fruits for counting games.

differentiation.support: Count only three fruits and say each number as the fruit goes in.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to count five fruits into the basket and then take away two and say how many are left.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: How many fruits are in the basket?
Can you put in three fruits?

expectedOutcomes: Counts up to five objects into a basket
Says how many in a game
lessons.conclusion: Pretend to carry the basket home from the market. Say "Five fruits. Thank you!"
lessons.homeConnection: Count fruits at home, such as five oranges in a bowl, when helping to wash them.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "count five toy fruits into a basket and say how many" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: How many now?
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will count a group, see one object added or removed, and say how many now.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can say the numbers to five in rhymes and count up to three objects by touching each one.
lessons.starter: Put three cups on a tray and ask "How many?" Then add a cup behind your back and say "Something changed. Let us count again."
teacherActivities: Show three cups, count them, then add one in front of the children. Say "Now count again."
Remove one cup and ask "How many now?"
Cover the cups with a cloth, lift it and ask "How many now?" Let them check by counting.
Let a child be the teacher: add or remove a cup and ask the group.
learnerActivities: Children count and say "four".
Children count and say "three".
Children count and give the new number.
Child changes the cups and the group counts.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show three cups, count them, then add one in front of the children. Say "Now count again." Children: Children count and say "four".
Step 2. Teacher: Remove one cup and ask "How many now?" Children: Children count and say "three".
Step 3. Teacher: Cover the cups with a cloth, lift it and ask "How many now?" Let them check by counting. Children: Children count and give the new number.
Step 4. Teacher: Let a child be the teacher: add or remove a cup and ask the group. Children: Child changes the cups and the group counts.

practical.title: Change and count
steps: Give each pair a tray with up to five cups.
One child adds or removes a cup while the other covers their eyes.
The partner counts and says how many now.
practical.safety: Use unbreakable cups and keep them on the tray; supervise to keep cups out of mouths.

differentiation.support: Change by one cup only between two and three.
differentiation.extension: Change by two cups and ask the child to say how many were added or removed.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: How many cups now?
questions.expected: The correct number after the change.

questions.question: Did I add or take away?
questions.expected: Child points or says add or take away.

lessons.conclusion: Gather the cups and count them one last time together, saying the final number.
lessons.homeConnection: Ask "how many now?" when a biscuit is eaten or added at snack time.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "count a group, see one object added or removed, and say how many now" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Collect five
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will collect up to five objects while moving and count them.
successCriteria: Collects the number of objects asked for
Counts them aloud or with fingers
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can say the numbers to five in rhymes and count up to three objects by touching each one.
resources: Ten soft balls scattered on the floor
lessons.starter: Roll the soft balls around the room. Say "Let us go on a ball hunt. How many balls can we collect in the basket?"
teacherActivities: Say "Collect three balls." Pick up each ball and say its number as it goes in the basket.
Say "Now collect five." Watch as each child collects and counts.
Ask "How many are in the basket?" and let the group check by counting.
Change the task: "Collect four balls and take them to the shelf."
learnerActivities: Children collect three balls and count aloud.
Children collect five balls and say the numbers.
Children count again and say the final number.
Child collects four balls, counts, and carries them to the shelf.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Say "Collect three balls." Pick up each ball and say its number as it goes in the basket. Children: Children collect three balls and count aloud.
Step 2. Teacher: Say "Now collect five." Watch as each child collects and counts. Children: Children collect five balls and say the numbers.
Step 3. Teacher: Ask "How many are in the basket?" and let the group check by counting. Children: Children count again and say the final number.
Step 4. Teacher: Change the task: "Collect four balls and take them to the shelf." Children: Child collects four balls, counts, and carries them to the shelf.

practical.title: Ball hunt
steps: Scatter ten soft balls around the room.
Call a number from one to five.
Children collect that many and place them in a basket.
practical.safety: Use soft balls larger than a fist and keep the floor free of other objects. Children walk, not run.

differentiation.support: Collect only two balls at a time with an adult beside the child.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to collect five balls without help and tell the group how many.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: How many balls are in your basket?
questions.expected: The number asked for, up to five.

lessons.conclusion: Tip the balls out and roll them back to the middle while saying the numbers.
lessons.homeConnection: Ask your child to collect five spoons or five toys and count them as they bring them.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "collect up to five objects while moving and count them" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Counting to five stations
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will show they can count to five and say how many at three stations.
successCriteria: Says how many for up to five
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can say the numbers to five in rhymes and count up to three objects by touching each one.
lessons.starter: Show the three stations and say "Today we count to five at each station. Remember to touch each one."
teacherActivities: Rotate groups every four minutes and observe one station closely.
At each station ask "How many?" and watch for one touch per object.
Ask "How many now?" after adding or removing an object at one station.
Note each child’s level and take photographs.
learnerActivities: Children count at each station.
Child counts and answers.
Child recounts and says the new number.
Children tidy at the signal.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Rotate groups every four minutes and observe one station closely. Children: Children count at each station.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station ask "How many?" and watch for one touch per object. Children: Child counts and answers.
Step 3. Teacher: Ask "How many now?" after adding or removing an object at one station. Children: Child recounts and says the new number.
Step 4. Teacher: Note each child’s level and take photographs. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Station circuit
practical.safety: Remove small items and keep walkways clear.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner at each station.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to be the counting leader.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: touches one object for each number; counts to three reliably and to five with support; says how many with the last number.

questions.question: How many fruits?
questions.expected: The correct number up to five.

questions.question: Can you count the blocks again?
questions.expected: Child counts again and gets the same number.

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 3
lessons.conclusion: Count the children in the circle together, up to five at a time.
lessons.homeConnection: Count five things a day with your child.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "show they can count to five and say how many at three stations" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
